title: Physics bug in pixel-perfect games
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.4.1 stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7283) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-10105F CPU @ 3.70GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

Working on a pixelart project in Godot 4 stable, and I have noticed that there are physics glitches in characterbody and rigidbody. It's as if the object is “shaking.” It's very noticeable since the project is pixel art and set to a low resolution (1080p/4). I couldn't find any information about this glitch, so I asked ChatGPT, and it said it was something about “micro-movements” and that it can be fixed by adding “position=position.round()” in physics_process.

This bug is not in Godot 3.x

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09f8acbb-333c-40f9-94ee-7f110f9ceab9)

### Steps to reproduce

Use characterbody2d and move it, or rigidbody2d and apply impulse, using pixel-perfect settings (viewport, transforms snap to pixel, low-resolution canvas)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Use characterbody2d and move it, or rigidbody2d and apply impulse, using pixel-perfect settings (viewport, transforms snap to pixel, low-resolution canvas)

[test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20542237/test.zip)
